pageCache.pageTitle: Rydes Hill Prep School & Nursery | Private School Guildford | Rydes Hill Preparatory School & Nursery
pageCache.text:
At Rydes Hill, we offer outstanding education and pastoral care for children aged 6 months to 11 years, combining academic ambition with a nurturing, family-focused environment. We believe that happy children thrive, and our warm, inclusive atmosphere ensures every child feels valued and part of the Rydes Hill family.
Our highly qualified teachers are dedicated to helping each child grow into a caring, confident, and capable learner. With a strong emphasis on personal development and academic excellence, we lay the foundations for future success and inspire a lifelong love of learning in every child.
Following the recent announcement of the merger between Rydes Hill and Tormead, we are pleased to announce that Rydes Hill Prep School will become fully co-educational in Year 3 from September 2027, followed by Year 4 in September 2028. To find out more visit our Prep page.
Take a look at our prospectus to get a glimpse of life at Rydes Hill:
"From the beginning, what has stood out most is the quality of the teaching."
"Rydes Hill Nursery really was the making of our son! The compassion, care and support that he received, brought him out of his shell and has shaped who he is today. The Nursery staff were always available and approachable were there any questions or concerns and we loved receiving updates of his learning and progress via Tapestry!"
"What has meant the most to me as a parent is seeing how happy my daughter is at RH. She goes into school with confidence and comes home full of stories, curiosity, and pride in what she’s learning and the friends she made."
"As parents, we feel listened to, and that our feedback genuinely matters, which creates a real sense of trust and partnership."
"Our son has transformed since joining Rydes Hill. He’s more confident and happier than ever. He loves all the outdoor activities and is always excited to tell us about all the new things he’s been learning. Thank you to the amazing teachers and support staff who work so hard to give the children the very best".
"Teachers expectations are aspirational and their lessons are well-considered to challenge pupils while providing appropriate support whenever necessary."
Now Welcoming Babies From 6 Months
We are delighted to announce that, from Summer 2026, we are extending our first-class nursery provision to include dedicated care for our youngest learners.

pageCache.pageTitle: Specialist teachers | Rydes Hill Preparatory School & Nursery
pageCache.text:
Specialist teachers
At Rydes Hill, we are delighted to provide specialist teaching in music, sport, science, french, IT and Forest School. Our specialist teachers complement the instruction of our form teachers and bring numerous benefits to the educational experience of our children, ultimately helping to solidify our pupils love for learning. Just a few of these benefits are listed below:
Expertise:
Our specialist teacher’s in-depth knowledge and expertise in their respective subjects allows for the delivery of first-class teaching which provides pupils with an enhanced understanding of these subjects.
Enhanced learning opportunities:
The variety offered to our pupils via specialist teaching provides additional learning experiences and opportunities that go beyond the core subjects taught by our excellent form teachers. Their specialisms help to broaden our pupils' horizons by facilitating their discovery of new interests. Additionally, our form and specialist teachers frequently collaborate, creating cross-curricular learning possibilities that present a whole range of additional benefits.
Improved skill development:
Our specialist teachers focus on developing skills that are specific to their subject areas, contributing to the holistic development and education of our pupils. Furthermore, they are easily able to identify a pupil’s additional skills or needs in their specialist area and can offer supplementary coaching, encouragement and support where appropriate.
Overall, our specialist teachers work to build on the exceptional work of our form teachers by offering an additional dimension to our teaching framework and supplementing our pupils' intellectual, physical and creative development.

pageCache.pageTitle: Speech and drama | Rydes Hill Preparatory School & Nursery
pageCache.text:
Drama and the Performing Arts
Drama and the performing arts are a vibrant and vital part of life at Rydes Hill. Learning to stand up and talk in public, or perform in any way, is a invaluable life skill and even those who do not come to it naturally, develop an ease in standing up in front of others.
All children are introduced to Speech and Drama from Reception. Throughout their time with us, our pupils have ample opportunity to perform a variety of material via performance poetry, sketches, musicals, plays and solo performances in front of their peers, the whole school, parents and family.
Drama is a flourishing subject at Rydes Hill and we love to see our confident and articulate children moving on to the next stage of their education. Many are awarded drama scholarships but, above all, they have a lifetime interest and enthusiasm for drama and the performing arts.

pageCache.pageTitle: Music | Rydes Hill Preparatory School & Nursery
pageCache.text:
Music at Rydes Hill
Music and the performing arts are a vibrant and vital part of life at Rydes Hill.
Within our thriving music department the children are encouraged to discover their musical potential and realise their natural talents. We aim to foster children’s enjoyment and understanding of music from a young age with all pupils in Pre-Prep given the opportunity to learn the violin, a wind and a brass instrument.
The main aim is to foster children's enjoyment and understanding of music through practical application and active involvement in a wide range of musical activities, both in and out of class lesson time. The music, drama and ballet departments work closely together to encourage a high standard of performance throughout the year.
Class music lessons
During class music lessons children learn to develop their vocal and instrumental skills, to improvise and compose and become familiar with a wide range of music, past and present. Our Head of Music, teaches all children at Rydes Hill.
Each class receives two forty minute music lessons per week, held in the spacious and well-equipped Music Room in the fabulous Performing Arts Centre. Music lessons are linked to other areas of the curriculum that are being covered in class.
Viva violins scheme
In Year 2 every child has the opportunity to learn the violin as part of the music curriculum. The ‘Viva Violins’ scheme is taught by our specialist violin teacher, and all tuition is free for the entire academic year.
Individual tuition
Children in pre-prep will have the opportunity to learn an instrument of their choice. We are exceptionally lucky at Rydes Hill in having an outstanding team of visiting peripatetic music teachers. Their aim is to inspire and encourage the children to reach their full musical potential.
Tuition is currently available on piano, recorder, voice and all string instruments.

pageCache.pageTitle: Academic & Scholarships | Rydes Hill Preparatory School & Nursery
pageCache.text:
Academic & Scholarships
Academic
Strong foundations. Ambitious futures.
At Rydes Hill Prep, academic excellence is about inspiring every child to achieve their personal best. Through high-quality teaching, ambitious expectations and individual support, we nurture confident learners who are curious, resilient and ready to embrace challenges.
Small class sizes mean every child is known as an individual. Our teachers understand how each pupil learns best, providing the encouragement, challenge and guidance needed to help them flourish academically while developing a genuine love of learning.
Learning with purpose
Our broad and balanced curriculum provides pupils with a strong foundation across every subject while encouraging them to think critically, ask questions and make meaningful connections in their learning.
Lessons are carefully planned to stretch and inspire, enabling children to build knowledge, deepen understanding and develop the confidence to tackle new challenges independently. Learning is purposeful, engaging and enriched through practical experiences, educational visits and specialist teaching, ensuring that every child is encouraged to fulfil their potential.
Challenge and support
We believe that every child should experience the right level of challenge. By recognising individual strengths, interests and aspirations, our teachers tailor their approach to ensure pupils are supported when they need guidance and challenged when they are ready to take the next step.
Children are encouraged to persevere, embrace mistakes as opportunities for learning and develop the resilience needed to succeed both inside and beyond the classroom.
Preparing for senior school success
The Prep years are an important time of growth and discovery. As children become increasingly independent learners, they develop the academic skills, confidence and character needed to thrive at senior school.
Alongside excellent teaching, we work closely with families to ensure every child is prepared for the next stage of their educational journey. By the end of Year 6, our pupils leave Rydes Hill with strong academic foundations, growing independence and the confidence to embrace ambitious futures.
STEM
Introduction - Inspiring curiosity. Encouraging innovation.
At Rydes Hill Prep, STEM learning is about far more than acquiring knowledge. It is about asking questions, solving problems and developing the confidence to explore the world with curiosity and creativity.
Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics are taught through a varied curriculum, with Science, Mathematics, Computing and Design Technology each taught as discrete subjects. As pupils progress through the Prep years, they learn to make connections across these disciplines, applying their knowledge and skills to real-life challenges and practical investigations.
Learning through discovery
Our well-equipped science laboratory provides an inspiring environment where children learn through hands-on investigation. Regular practical experiments encourage pupils to question, predict, test and evaluate, developing scientific thinking alongside a genuine enthusiasm for discovery.
Science learning extends beyond the laboratory. Our school grounds and Forest School programme provide rich opportunities to explore the natural world, reinforcing classroom learning through first-hand experiences. As an Eco-School, sustainability and environmental responsibility are woven throughout school life, helping pupils develop an understanding of the role they can play in caring for the world around them.
Technology with purpose
Technology is thoughtfully integrated into learning, equipping children with the digital skills they will need for the future. With access to both iPads and laptops, pupils learn to use technology confidently, creatively and responsibly.
Our dedicated STEM Hub provides a collaborative space where innovation comes to life. From coding and programming with Micro and robotics to designing and creating with our 3D printer, children are encouraged to think critically, experiment with ideas and embrace new technologies with confidence.
A wider world of opportunity
As part of the Tormead family of schools, our pupils benefit from exciting opportunities beyond the Prep classroom. Specialist Science teachers from Tormead visit Rydes Hill throughout the year to deliver inspiring lessons that deepen understanding, spark curiosity and introduce children to new scientific concepts and ideas.
Learning is further enriched through visiting speakers, local field studies and STEM-focused experiences that connect classroom learning with the wider world, helping pupils see the relevance and possibilities of STEM in everyday life.
Leadership opportunities also play an important role. In Year 6, pupils can become STEM Ambassadors, encouraging younger children, promoting curiosity across the school and developing the confidence, responsibility and communication skills that will support them throughout their education.
At Rydes Hill, STEM is about nurturing inquisitive minds, resilient thinkers and confident problem solvers who are prepared to embrace the opportunities and challenges of an ever-changing world.

pageCache.pageTitle: Specialist Provision | Rydes Hill Preparatory School & Nursery
pageCache.text:
Specialist Provision
Performing Arts
Inspiring creativity. Building confidence.
At Rydes Hill Prep, specialist teaching enriches every child's learning experience, encouraging them to discover new interests, develop their talents and grow in confidence. Whether performing on stage, creating a piece of artwork or exploring a new creative skill, pupils are inspired to express themselves and strive for excellence.
The performing arts are at the heart of life at Rydes Hill, providing every child with opportunities to develop confidence, creativity and self-expression.
Pupils enjoy weekly specialist lessons in both Music and Drama, where they build technical skills while developing communication, collaboration and performance confidence. Alongside the curriculum, a wide range of peripatetic music tuition enables children to learn individual instruments and pursue their musical interests.
Led by our dedicated Director of Music, the department offers a rich programme of concerts, productions, showcases and performances throughout the year. Whether performing as part of a choir, taking centre stage in a school production or sharing their talents at a recital, every child is encouraged to participate and experience the joy of performing before an audience.
Beyond the classroom, our extensive co-curricular programme provides even more opportunities for pupils to develop their passions. Ballet and musical theatre classes enable children to refine their performance skills, build confidence and enjoy working collaboratively, while discovering the excitement and discipline of the performing arts.
These experiences help pupils develop resilience, teamwork and self-belief - qualities that stay with them long after the final curtain falls.
Art and creativity
Creativity is celebrated throughout the school and woven into the fabric of everyday learning.
Weekly Art lessons encourage pupils to experiment with a wide range of materials, techniques and artistic styles, developing both technical skills and imaginative thinking. Children are inspired to take creative risks, explore new ideas and take pride in their individual achievements.
Learning extends beyond the classroom through visits to galleries and museums, where pupils encounter inspiring works of art and broaden their understanding of artistic traditions and contemporary practice.
Our vibrant annual art exhibition showcases pupils' work, celebrating creativity, originality and progress across the school. It is a highlight of the school calendar and reflects our belief that every child has the potential to think creatively and express themselves with confidence.
At Rydes Hill, creativity is not confined to the arts. It is nurtured across the curriculum, encouraging children to become curious thinkers, imaginative problem solvers and confident learners, prepared for the opportunities that lie ahead.
Sport
Sport at Rydes Hill: Engage. Thrive. Excel.
Our mission is to provide sport for all: creating an inclusive, ambitious environment in which every boy and girl can participate with confidence, discover activities they enjoy and fulfil their potential. Whether pupils are taking their first steps in sport or aspiring to compete at the highest level, our programme enables them to engage, thrive and excel.
From Year 3, every pupil benefits from more than three hours of dedicated curriculum sport each week, comprising a PE lesson, a Games afternoon and a swimming lesson. This significant commitment reflects the important role that sport plays in developing healthy, confident and well-rounded young people.
Outstanding facilities
Games afternoons provide pupils with access to the state-of-the-art Urnfield Sports Ground, where they can enjoy hockey, football, cricket and athletics within a first-class sporting environment. Netball and tennis are delivered on the school’s on-site courts.
PE lessons also take place across Rydes Hill’s on-site sports hall, playing field and two full-size netball and tennis courts.
Building confident and capable young people
Boys and girls are taught together during PE lessons, which focus on developing strong foundations in physical literacy. Through carefully designed units, pupils develop speed, agility, strength, coordination and balance alongside transferable qualities such as communication, teamwork, leadership, resilience, decision-making and problem-solving.
Our aim is not simply to develop better performers, but to nurture confident young people who understand the value of physical activity and are equipped to enjoy sport throughout their lives.
An ambitious and varied Games programme
During Games afternoons, boys and girls are taught separately, allowing the programme to provide appropriate sporting pathways, focused coaching and a breadth of opportunities.
The boys’ seasonal programme comprises:
Boys initially undertake a six-week block in the principal sport, ensuring that every pupil develops a strong foundation. They may then choose to continue with that sport or broaden their experience through one of the alternative activities.
The girls’ seasonal programme comprises:
This structure combines high-quality teaching in the school’s principal sports with meaningful choice, enabling pupils to explore their interests and develop across a range of activities.
Opportunities beyond the curriculum
Our extensive co-curricular programme enables pupils to develop their skills, stay active and represent the school. Autumn and Spring activities include hockey, netball, football, gymnastics and dance, while summer offers athletics, tennis and cricket.
A broad programme of fixtures and festivals gives pupils of all abilities the opportunity to compete at an appropriate level. Carefully matched competition creates positive experiences for every child, while aspiring performers can progress to IAPS, county, regional and national events.
Specialist teaching and coaching
The programme is delivered by a dedicated and experienced team of PE teachers and sports professionals. Provision at Rydes Hill is led by Danielle Fellowes Freeman, Lead PE Practitioner, and overseen by George Pettitt, Director of Sport.
Together, the team is committed to providing inspirational teaching, expert coaching and positive sporting experiences that enable every pupil to develop confidence, character and a lifelong enjoyment of physical activity.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pastoral care | Rydes Hill Preparatory School & Nursery
pageCache.text:
At Rydes Hill, outstanding pastoral care is central to everything we do. We understand how crucial it is to continually support the wellbeing of our children and staff so they can thrive. We are proud to have built a culture of support, inclusion and kindness. In addition to our interactive and comprehensive life skills sessions, we have additional initiatives to support children who are finding things tough.
Emotional Literacy Support
If we feel that a pupil would benefit from emotional literacy support we will inform their parents that we would like to invite them to come for some sessions. Parents may also speak to their class teacher or a member of the senior leadership team if they would like their child to be considered. Sessions are complimentary and run 1:1.
Special Educational Needs
If a pupil has additional needs in supporting their academic progress, we can offer individual or group teaching assistant support for an extra fee. If we suspect that your child would benefit from extra support or has additional needs, we will speak to you at the earliest opportunity to discuss options. If you have concerns about your child, please speak to their class teacher in the first instance. If required, your child’s class teacher will arrange a conversation with our SENCO.
Meet Cody - Our School Dog
Cody is our much-loved Miniature Poodle and an important member of the Rydes Hill School community. At four years old, Cody is a friendly, gentle and hypoallergenic dog who brings comfort, joy and companionship to children and staff across the school.
Cody began his puppy training as soon as he had completed all of his vaccinations and later continued his training with Danielle Tree at Guildford Dog School. With his excellent manners and calm nature, Cody has become a regular “Employee of the Month” and takes his role at school very seriously.
Cody actually grew up alongside the children at Rydes Hill School. Their love, patience and attention helped shape him into the wonderful dog he is today. He enjoys spending time with pupils throughout the school day and is always happy to join lessons, pastoral sessions and Forest School activities.
Cody plays an important role in supporting children’s wellbeing. Spending time with him can help pupils feel calm, safe and supported. He has helped several children overcome their fears of dogs, practise their speaking and reading skills, and build confidence. On days when things feel a little tough, Cody is always ready with a wagging tail and a reassuring presence to help children feel happier and more settled.
Like any good school dog, Cody also loves to play. His favourite games include finding hidden toys, playing fetch with a ball and searching for treats. He is also quite the gymnast and can perform a very impressive vault!
School dogs like Cody can have a wonderful impact on school life. They can help reduce stress and anxiety, encourage positive social interactions, and support children’s emotional wellbeing. For many pupils, spending time with Cody provides a calm moment in a busy day and helps create a warm, nurturing school environment.
Cody loves coming into school each day and being surrounded by the children who care so much about him. He is a very special member of our school family.

pageCache.pageTitle: Forest School and outdoor learning | Rydes Hill Preparatory School & Nursery
pageCache.text:
Forest School and outdoor learning
For a long time, research has proven that there is a positive correlation between access and exposure to fresh air and enhanced learning outcomes. As a consequence, we dedicate a portion of our curriculum to being immersed in the great outdoors. From Nursery onwards, all Rydes Hill pupils benefit and enjoy outdoor adventures in our dedicated woodland Forest School. Additionally, we have recently built a new outdoor classroom that enables our pupils to benefit from outdoor learning, whatever the weather.
Forest School is an educational approach that emphasises learning and personal development in natural outdoor environments, typically woodland areas and forests. The overarching philosophy of Forest School is to provide children with frequent opportunities to engage with and experience nature in a hands-on manner. The overall aim is to encourage a child’s deep connection with the natural world, promote independence and encourage curiosity and creativity.
Forest School activities are typically child-centred and play-based, led by specially trained Forest School teachers. Activities include den building, nature walks, fire building, plant and mini beast identification, storytelling and arts and crafts using natural materials found in the environment. At Rydes Hill, we endeavour to cross our Forest School classes with other subjects in our cross-curricular programme. This helps to maximise a child’s time outside and also provides an additional and alternative dimension to other lessons.
We find that there are numerous benefits to offering Forest School as part of our curriculum. Forest School lessons can help to enhance physical skills such as coordination and balance as well as emotional and social skills, including teamwork, problem solving and resilience. Furthermore, Forest School and teaching outdoors also promotes an understanding and appreciation for the natural world, environmental awareness and a sense of stewardship.

pageCache.pageTitle: Sport | Rydes Hill Preparatory School & Nursery
pageCache.text:
Sport for All
At Rydes Hill, every child benefits from a vibrant PE and Games programme alongside a wide range of co-curricular sports clubs. These opportunities develop core skills, enhance physical literacy, and inspire a lifelong love of sport and physical activity. Whether in lessons or clubs, all sessions are led by specialist PE and Games teachers who bring energy and expertise to help every child discover their passion for being active.
From Nursery through to Year 2, all pupils have access to a a rich and varied programme of physical activity. This includes a weekly PE lesson on Mondays, a Games lesson on Tuesdays, and up to three lunchtime co-curricular sports clubs from Wednesday to Friday. Reception to Year 2 children also benefit from weekly swimming lessons at Surrey Sports Park on Friday afternoons.
Physical Education and sport are integral to our broader curriculum at Rydes Hill. While developing fundamental movement skills and nurturing a lifelong love of sport, we also use physical activity to support pupil wellbeing. Through sport, children learn respect, kindness, empathy, teamwork, and healthy habits that help them thrive both in and beyond the classroom. We actively encourage a growth mindset, building confidence, resilience, and a willingness to embrace challenges. We recognise the valuable, transferable skills that sport brings to each child’s learning journey.
Physical Education and Games
Physical Education lessons are designed to develop physical literacy by building fundamental movement patterns, motor skills, and physical capabilities essential for healthy growth. Pupils take part in age-appropriate 6 or 12-week units, each tailored to their stage of development and focused on key skill areas, including:
· Balance and Strength
· Agility and Movement
· Hand-Eye Coordination
Games lessons at Rydes Hill focus on developing key motor and ball-handling skills, along with the basic principles of attacking and defending, in an engaging and supportive setting. These lessons provide a strong foundation for pupils to build confidence and competence in team sports and physical activity as they move through the school.
Pupils follow carefully planned 6 or 12-week units, tailored to their stage of development. Each unit targets a specific area, including:
· Ball and Movement Fundamentals
· Attacking Principles
· Defensive Principles
· Striking and Fielding Games
· Net and Wall Games
Co-Curricular Sport
Weekly sports clubs are offered to all pupils from Reception to Year 2, running during lunchtimes and led by specialist PE teachers and qualified sports coaches. These sessions are designed to reinforce and build upon the skills developed in PE and Games lessons.
Clubs are open to all pupils, with no additional cost—fees are included within the annual school tuition, with the exception of gymnastics at Tormead which is charged at an additional cost. Lunchtime clubs cover a range of sports and activities throughout the week:
· Wednesday: Tennis & Ball Skills
· Thursday: Gymnastics
· Friday: Games Skills (termly focus varies—e.g. netball, football, hockey, cricket)
Rydes Hill Spring Clubs Timetable 2025 26
Swimming
All pupils from Reception to Year 2 attend weekly swimming lessons at Surrey Sports Park on Friday afternoons, delivered by experienced and highly qualified instructors. The programme begins by building water confidence and key aquatic skills, before moving on to the development of all four strokes. The focus is on ensuring every child feels happy, safe, and confident in the water, with the ultimate aim of enabling all pupils to swim 25 metres unaided by the end of Year 2. A high staff-to-pupil ratio supports strong progress for every swimmer, regardless of their starting point.
Looking Ahead
With the exciting announcement that Rydes Hill will become fully co-educational, beginning with the introduction of Year 3 in September 2027, we are delighted by the opportunity to expand and enrich our sports provision.
In partnership with Tormead, we will have access to the excellent facilities at Urnfield Sports Ground, including extensive grass pitches for cricket and football, state-of-the-art cricket nets, an all-weather hockey pitch, and a six-lane 400m athletics track with full jumping and throwing facilities. In addition, we will benefit from use of Tormead’s on-site facilities—just a 10-minute bus ride away—which feature four netball and tennis courts, a sprung-floor gymnasium, and a large indoor sports hall.
Together with the extensive grounds at Rydes Hill, this partnership creates an exceptional platform for sport. It will enrich the experience of all pupils by broadening curriculum sport opportunities, expanding the range of co-curricular clubs available to all ages and abilities, and establishing a inclusive fixtures programme. Pupils will have regular chances to represent the school and compete at local, regional, and national levels across athletics, cricket, gymnastics, football, hockey, netball, swimming, and tennis.
Contact for PE and Sport
As a proud member of the Tormead Family, the PE, Games, and sports club provision at Rydes Hill is carefully overseen by Tormead’s experienced PE and Sports Department, led by Director of Sport, George Pettitt. For further information about our PE and sports offering at Rydes Hill, please feel free to contact him at gpettitt@tormeadschool.org.uk.

Our close-knit community, often described as the Rydes Hill family, is built on genuine relationships between staff, pupils and parents. Together, we create a nurturing space where every child can thrive.
